description: This USGS Fact Sheet 2025-3057, first posted on 23 April 2026, covers uranium deposits, production and resources, market dynamics and supply chain risks. It opens with the rising interest in nuclear power, including small modular reactors for remote areas, industry and AI data centres, and notes that the U.S. Department of Energy received 2.7 billion dollars in 2024 to strengthen domestic uranium production and the fuel supply chain. The text explains that uranium occurs in at least 15 deposit types, of which sandstone-hosted deposits, unconformity-related deposits and deposits in intrusive igneous rocks are the most productive globally, describes uses of uranium, and recounts the price path from the 2011 Fukushima accident to a 17-year spot high of 106 dollars per pound of U3O8 in January 2024. It is published as a PDF of 10.5 MB, HTML and XML, with a National Geologic Map Database index page. Coverage is global with a U.S. focus. Access: free. Caveats: a summary fact sheet, not a mine-level dataset. It suits nuclear fuel supply and capacity planning studies, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
